findings.reason: the pruning rule is a stated part of the deliverable and its failure mode is a silently missing row, the exact class of defect the section exists to remove, so the done-when must add an end-then-re-grant case for the mechanism to be measured.
findings.text: §23's deliverable declares "a claim is pruned once its lift has ended and the end row has been drawn", but the done-when tests only grant, end, a second lift id, a different session and the negative control; it never drives a lift that ends and is granted again, so a prune that removes only the end claim while leaving the grant claim in place — silently suppressing the next grant on the pane — passes the gate

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_lift_row` (`reckon/crew/lift_watch.py:170`), `_watch_transition`, `RowPolicy._lift_groups` (`reckon/crew/ticker.py:1177`) and `follow_checkpoint` all resolve, and §23 carries no href.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §23's done-when measures the grant, the end, a second lift id, a different session and a declared negative control, but it never exercises the pruning rule the same deliverable states, so a broken prune passes the gate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate is a test module under `tests/` and the control is logged under the run directory, both durable paths in the repository and the crew home.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach the symbols (`lift_id`, `_lift_row`) or the prose, which states the mechanism in the code's own terms.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence (`_feed_lift` at `reckon/crew/ticker.py:1684` draws a grant unconditionally, so each of the session's followers draws the one grant), the mechanism produces the done-when, and the caller is named (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py`, the follower's print path).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, a lift row drawn once per session pane; the added `lift_id` field and the claim are its means, and run rows are explicitly left unchanged.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §23 declares "runs after §22" (which is `done`, so no edge is needed), its write paths (`lift_watch.py`, `ticker.py`, `crew_follow_commands.py`) collide with no live claim, and its statement that it does not touch `recovery_watch.py` (which §14 writes) holds.
